pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); 7-day trial; auto-renews until canceled
pricing.hiddenCosts: Custom events and API calls count toward pageviews; extra sites cost an additional unpublished fee. Two consecutive months over the limit trigger an offered upgrade rather than immediate throttling.

verdictSummary: A simple privacy analytics clone is very buildable; the paid service is hosted compliance posture, uptime, data retention, and polished reporting.
coreLoopDIY: Collect pageviews/events via JS, aggregate metrics, show simple dashboards, and send reports.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to avoid maintaining analytics infrastructure and privacy copy themselves.

priorArt.name: Umami
priorArt.desc: Open-source privacy-focused analytics platform and practical DIY alternative.

alternatives.name: GoatCounter
alternatives.desc: A smaller privacy dashboard for people who truly meant simple.

facts.install: Create a hosted account or run the single static binary or Docker image
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted instance uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL; the hosted service stores analytics on GoatCounter's infrastructure and supports JSON and CSV exports
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers fewer polished goals, events, reports, team controls and support than Fathom's managed product.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted use; self-hosting needs a reachable binary or container plus a public URL and TLS

alternatives.name: Plausible Community Edition
alternatives.desc: The closest philosophical match, except you operate the Compose file.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose installer
facts.dataFormat: Account and configuration records live in PostgreSQL and analytics events live in ClickHouse on the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: The philosophy is close, but the user must run PostgreSQL and ClickHouse and loses Fathom's managed operations and support.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, roughly 2 GB of RAM, a domain with DNS and TLS, and backups for PostgreSQL and ClickHouse

alternatives.name: Umami
alternatives.desc: Simple privacy analytics with enough events and goals to avoid paying for simplicity.

facts.install: Create an Umami Cloud account or deploy the Node application with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted deployment stores analytics and account data in PostgreSQL; Umami Cloud stores it in Umami's managed service
facts.gapVsPaid: It is less deliberately minimal and, when self-hosted, lacks Fathom's managed reliability and support.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted signup; self-hosting requires Docker or Node hosting and a PostgreSQL database

notes: Useful because several analytics apps are genuinely cloneable now.
prompt:
Build me a privacy-first web analytics service to replace Fathom Analytics. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, one small app I deploy on my VPS behind
  Caddy or nginx.
- The tracker: a single script tag under 2 KB that sends pageview beacons
  (path, referrer, screen width) with navigator.sendBeacon. No cookies.
- Count unique visitors without storing personal data: hash IP + user agent
  with a salt that rotates daily, then drop the raw values.
- Filter obvious bots against a user-agent blocklist before counting.
- Dashboard page: pageviews, uniques, top pages, top referrers over 7/30/365
  days, one Chart.js line chart plus tables. Protected by a single bearer
  token from .env, no user accounts.
- Retention: raw events kept 30 days, daily rollups kept forever, pruned by a
  nightly node-cron job.
- No cookies, no personal data at rest, no telemetry of its own.
- Out of scope: email reports, team seats, billing. One site, or a short site
  list in config.
- README: deploy steps, adding the script tag, and a plain note that this is
  polite analytics, not a legal compliance product.
